Definition: of uncertain affinity; roving (as a tramp), i.e. (by implication) an impostor or misleader; --deceiver, seducing.
BiblicalUsage: Planos is a deceiver, a rover, one who wanders and leads others wandering. The chief priests called Jesus that deceiver in Matthew 27:63, and John warns that many deceivers are entered into the world in 2 John 1:7. Paul says seducing spirits will speak in the latter times in 1 Timothy 4:1, and that apostles are counted as deceivers, yet true, in 2 Corinthians 6:8.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the world calls the truth a deception and deception the truth. I would rather be counted a deceiver with Paul than be believed with the crowd.
